title: Development of split-root assays for loblolly pine seedlings to study ectomycorrhizal symbioses
author: Rose, Frank, et al.
materials: 60 mm x 15 mm sterile plastic Petri dishes

1.Prior to seedling transplant, sterilize one clone collar and one 250 ml beaker per seedling:a.Open rubber foam clone collars slightly at perforations and submerge in 90% ethanol for 10 min to sterilize.b.Remove collars from ethanol and place upright in sterile biosafety cabinet, with open perforations facing upward, under UV light for 1 h. After 1 h, lay collars flat to allow UV exposure on one side for 1 h, then turn over to expose the other side under UV for an additional 1 h.c.Gently squeeze each collar to check that ethanol has completely evaporated from pores in the foam rubber. Sterilized collars can be kept in a covered autoclaved container until transplant if necessary.2.In the same biosafety cabinet, add 200 ml of autoclaved N1 nutrient solution (Table S1, [15]) to each autoclaved 250 ml glass beaker.

steps.title: Sterilize clone collars
steps.instruction: Sterilize one clone collar per seedling using ethanol and UV light.

substeps.instruction: Open rubber foam clone collars slightly at perforations and submerge in 90% ethanol for 10 min.
Place collars upright in a sterile biosafety cabinet with open perforations facing upward under UV light for 1 h.
Lay collars flat and expose one side to UV light for 1 h, then turn over and expose the other side for an additional 1 h.
Gently squeeze each collar to ensure ethanol has completely evaporated from the foam rubber pores.
Store sterilized collars in a covered autoclaved container if necessary.

steps.title: Prepare nutrient solution beakers
steps.instruction: Prepare the hydroponic environment in a biosafety cabinet.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 ml of autoclaved N1 nutrient solution to each autoclaved 250 ml glass beaker.

steps.title: Inoculate ECM fungal liquid cultures
steps.instruction: Initiate liquid cultures of ECM fungus four weeks before seedling transplant.

substeps.instruction: Use a sterile 1 cm diameter cork borer to cut a plug from the advancing edge of mycelia growing on MMN agar medium (use YMG medium for H. cylindrosporum).
Transfer the plug using a sterile spatula into a sterile 100 ml culture jar containing 50 ml of autoclaved MMN liquid medium (or appropriate medium for the specific fungus).
Incubate the liquid culture jars in the dark at 26 °C for 4 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare fungal slurry inoculants
steps.instruction: Prepare the fungal slurry on the day of seedling transplant within a sterile cabinet.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the fungal thallus from the liquid culture jar into an autoclaved 100 ml glass beaker containing 40 ml of autoclaved N1 medium using a sterile spatula.
Gently swirl the thallus to rinse excess MMN medium, then remove the thallus.
Place the rinsed thallus into an autoclaved 100 ml glass beaker containing 80 ml of autoclaved N1 liquid nutrient solution.
Grind the thallus using an immersion blender with a sterile grinding tip until no large fragments remain, but stop before complete homogenization so small hyphal particles remain visible.
Stir the slurry rapidly with a sterile spatula and divide evenly into two 40 ml aliquots in two sterile 50 ml glass beakers.
Cap the beakers with sterile aluminium foil and keep at room temperature for inoculation.
